text: Drinking a glass of water puts the water in you. Jumping into a pool puts you in the water. That's the baptism in the Spirit.
explanation:
On the evening He rose, Jesus breathed on His disciples and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit." They were born again; the Spirit now lived in them. Yet weeks later He told the same disciples to wait in Jerusalem for "the Promise of the Father… you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now… you shall receive power."

Every believer has the Spirit within; you can't be born again without Him. But baptizo means to immerse. It's one thing for Him to be in you, and another for you to be immersed in Him, clothed with power to be His witness. That's not only something you do; it's something you become. If you've never received this gift, simply ask.

text: "They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak." The Spirit gives the words, but you do the speaking.
explanation:
Many people wait for the Holy Spirit to take over their mouths. But read carefully: "They began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance." The Spirit supplies the utterance; you voice it. He never possesses you or forces you; you can start and you can stop.

It's like the priests at the Jordan. The river didn't part until their feet touched the water. So after you've asked the Father for the Spirit, relax and begin to speak by faith. A trickle becomes a stream, and the stream becomes the "rivers of living water" Jesus promised.

text: "I thank my God I speak with tongues more than you all; yet in the church…" People quote the second half and skip the first.
explanation:
Paul told the Corinthians that in a church gathering he'd rather speak five words with understanding than ten thousand in a tongue, because no one can be taught by words they can't follow. But he began by saying he prayed in tongues more than all of them, and the Corinthians were hardly shy about it.

In private, praying in the Spirit edifies you and speaks mysteries to God. "I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the understanding." Do both. Often after a season of praying in tongues, Scripture opens up, your English prayers go straight to the heart of the matter, and the five words you speak carry power.

text: When you don't know what's troubling your child, pray in the Spirit. He knows exactly.
explanation:
You can see something's wrong with your teenager but can't put your finger on it. Your mind might pray around the edges. The Holy Spirit knows exactly what's happening: perhaps a loneliness that's settled on them even among friends. When you pray in tongues, He prays through you what you can't articulate.

Keep going until you sense a release. Often your prayers in English then begin to flow, and you find yourself praying for the very thing the Spirit has already been praying. And the promise for your children is that they "shall be taught by the Lord": by Him, not just about Him. "And great shall be the peace of your children."

text: "Be filled with the Spirit" is present tense: keep on being filled. The way? "Speaking… singing and making melody."
explanation:
Paul contrasts being drunk with wine with being filled with the Spirit. The command is continuous and passive: let yourself be filled, again and again. And your active part is in the next verse: "speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord." When you're down or under attack, start singing, start praying in the Spirit.

Notice what follows straight after: wives, husbands, children, parents. Ephesians teaches more on family life than any other letter of Paul, and it puts this constant filling right before it. Your marriage and your parenting need more than techniques; they need the Spirit flowing through you.

text: "Stir up the gift of God which is in you": fan it into flame. "For God has not given us a spirit of fear."
explanation:
The word for gift here isn't the one used for the Holy Spirit Himself; it's charisma, the word for the spiritual gifts. And "stir up" means to fan into flame, like fanning embers until the fire catches. The next verse is joined to it: "For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind."

Most gifts of the Spirit operate as He wills. Praying in tongues is the one you can start whenever you choose. On a Hanukkah menorah, the central servant candle lights all the others. Praying in the Spirit is like that: as you fan it into flame, fear leaves and power, love and a sound mind flow.

text: Know your wealth before your walk. You're seated with Christ; step down into your family like someone from heaven.
explanation:
Ephesians opens with your riches: chosen, forgiven "according to the riches of His grace," raised up and seated with Christ in heavenly places. Only then does it talk about how you walk, and how you treat your spouse and children. The world teaches marriage and parenting by technique. God starts by telling you who you are.

Imagine an angel living with your family for a month: there'd be a dignity about him, without any holier-than-thou attitude. Jesus, "knowing that the Father had given all things into His hands, and that He had come from God and was going to God," rose and washed His disciples' feet. When you know what you have, humble service carries glory.
